cd /home/john/mynotes/deterministic_equidistribution_theory
cat > /tmp/profile_remark.py <<'EOF'
s=open('finite_spectral_shadows.tex').read()
anchor=r"""proved here is the mechanism (\cref{lem:cert}), the failure of every
purely $3$-adic formulation (\cref{prop:notthreeadic}), and the exact
location of the remaining content."""
add=anchor+r"""

\begin{remark}[Counterexample profile]\label{rem:profile}
A counterexample to the Collatz conjecture, if it exists, must by the
present theorem stack be \emph{mean-critical}
($\frac1N\sum b_n=\log_23+o(1)$, else \cref{prop:meandescent}),
\emph{non-coboundary phase-biased} (\cref{thm:keystone}), jointly
$(2,3)$-adically coherent, and certificate-free at every level of the
mixed tower. The simplest symbolic models with these properties are
balanced low-letter words over $\{1,2\}$ with
$\Pr[b{=}1]=2-\log_23\approx0.415$ (Sturmian/Beatty type, slope
$2-\log_23$)---the critical analogues of the all-ones word, whose
$2$-adic point is $x=-1$. Direct realizability tests support the ghost
expectation: for twelve intercepts $\theta$ and prefixes of length
$800$ ($B_N=1268$), the unique residue class modulo $2^{B_N+1}$
realizing the Sturmian prefix has least positive representative of full
bit-length $\approx B_N$, wandering with the prefix and never
stabilizing---the signature of a mixed-adic ghost, not a positive
integer. For \emph{periodic} balanced traps the ghost exclusion is
precisely the classical cycle problem, where the archimedean negative
weight is supplied by linear forms in logarithms
($|2^B-3^p|\gg2^B/B^{C}$): joint-tower rigidity restricted to periodic
traps is thus partially within reach of existing transcendence
technology, and the genuinely new content of \cref{op:ctwo} is its
aperiodic, single-orbit analogue.
\end{remark}"""
assert anchor in s
s=s.replace(anchor,add,1)
open('finite_spectral_shadows.tex','w').write(s)
print("ok")
EOF
python3 /tmp/profile_remark.py
pdflatex -interaction=nonstopmode finite_spectral_shadows.tex >/tmp/fss.log 2>&1; pdflatex -interaction=nonstopmode finite_spectral_shadows.tex >/tmp/fss.log 2>&1
grep -E "^!" /tmp/fss.log | head -3; pdfinfo finite_spectral_shadows.pdf | grep Pages
ailog add --tool claude-code --level-hint 2 --text "dc_32 discussion turn: STURMIAN GHOST TEST + counterexample-profile remark (43pp). Test (sturmian_ghost.py): balanced critical {1,2}-words, slope alpha = 2-log2(3), P[b=1] = 0.415; for 12 intercepts theta, prefixes N=800 (B_N=1268): the unique class mod 2^{B_N+1} realizing the prefix has least positive representative of FULL bit-length ~B_N, ratio r/2^M wandering in (0,1), NO stabilization at any N in {100,200,400,800} => all 12 candidates are MIXED-ADIC GHOSTS (the critical analogue of the all-ones ghost x=-1), supporting dc_32's no-positive-counterexample expectation. Paper: rem:profile added (counterexample must be mean-critical + non-coboundary-biased + jointly coherent + certificate-free; simplest models = Sturmian {1,2}; ghost data; PERIODIC balanced traps = the classical cycle problem where BAKER (linear forms in logs, |2^B-3^p| >> 2^B/B^C) supplies the archimedean negative weight => joint-tower rigidity for periodic traps partially within existing transcendence technology; genuinely new content of op:ctwo = the aperiodic single-orbit analogue 'Baker along orbits'). KEY SYNTHESIS NOTED: the other Collatz project (lean4) has its deepest sorries in Baker.lean - both programs terminate at the same pair: transcendence input (periodic, available) + aperiodic deterministic rigidity (open)." 2>&1 | tail -1
ailog validate 2>&1 | tail -1
